featuredArticle.title: Navigating Corporate Restructuring and Mergers in 2026
featuredArticle.description: We are proud to work with a diverse range of businesses and organizations. Our client relationships reflect the trust, professionalism, and confidence placed in our legal expertise.
paragraphs: A branch office in Bangladesh acts as an extension of its foreign parent company, without creating a separate legal entity. This means the parent company remains fully liable for all debts, liabilities, and obligations arising from the branch's operations. Establishing a branch requires prior approval from the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA), followed by registration with the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC) under the Companies Act 1994. A branch may engage in commercial activities, such as invoicing and collecting payments locally, but only within the scope of activities approved by BIDA. Additionally, any outward remittance of profits or funds requires specific clearance and justification to the Inter-Ministerial Committee. While a branch allows for easier setup and winding-up procedures, its activities are tightly regulated by foreign exchange control laws, making it less flexible for businesses aiming to expand or diversify operations in Bangladesh.

Due to these limitations, many foreign investors instead choose to incorporate a local private limited company with foreign shareholding. Unlike a branch, a locally incorporated company enjoys greater operational autonomy, fewer regulatory restrictions on commercial activities, and broader access to incentives, tenders, joint ventures, and banking facilities. This structure allows for profit retention and reinvestment in Bangladesh, and provides a stronger platform for long-term growth, especially in sectors like technology, services, manufacturing, and trading. For foreign companies looking to scale operations or establish a significant local presence, forming a Bangladeshi company offers a more flexible and commercially advantageous route.

In addition, corporate restructuring demands rigorous due diligence on asset ownership, pending civil or labor disputes, and existing contractual covenants. M&A agreements must integrate robust indemnification clauses, representations and warranties, and post-closing integration protocols. Our corporate team ensures seamless clearance through BSEC, RJSC, and tax authorities, safeguarding shareholder value throughout every transaction milestone.

Furthermore, modern governance standards require alignment with anti-money laundering (AML) frameworks, environmental compliance guidelines, and minority shareholder protections. Structuring tailored voting pacts and board composition agreements avoids protracted deadlocks and preserves institutional stability.

At Basunia & Associates, our corporate advocates guide both domestic enterprises and global conglomerates through complex entity formations, regulatory licensing, and high-value acquisitions with unwavering precision.

We structure tailored cross-border contracts that mitigate geopolitical risks, guarantee enforceability before international arbitration tribunals, and ensure unbroken commercial execution.

paragraphs: Shareholder agreements establish the foundational equilibrium among investors, founders, and executive management. Clear pre-emption rights, tag-along and drag-along mechanisms, and reserved matter lists prevent deadlock and protect minority stakeholders.

Under Section 233 of the Companies Act 1994, minority shareholders possessing requisite thresholds may seek judicial redress against oppressive or prejudicial management actions. Structuring binding dispute mechanisms safeguards institutional stability.
Our team drafts comprehensive shareholder covenants and articles of association tailored to investor expectations and long-term capitalization strategies.
